user.title: Add a person
user.description: Add one person per phone. Home Assistant will create a private webhook for them — nothing to add to `configuration.yaml`, and no restart needed.

data_description.person: Just a label for the sensor and your charts. It doesn't have to be unique.
data_description.webhook_id: Leave empty unless you're using an older version of the app that asks you to type the ID by hand. This value is the only thing protecting the sensor, so make it unguessable — 8 to 64 letters, numbers, hyphens or underscores.

url.title: Which address should {person}'s phone use?

data_description.url_source: Home Assistant Cloud and External work from anywhere. Internal only works at home.
data_description.custom_url: Only used when you pick **Custom** above. Choose this if you reach Home Assistant through a reverse proxy, your own domain, DuckDNS or Tailscale — addresses Home Assistant can't discover on its own. Paste the same address you use in your browser; you can leave the webhook path off and it will be added for you.

connect.title: Connect {person}'s phone
connect.description:
Open **Steps Into HA** on {person}'s iPhone and scan this code.

If your version of the app doesn't have a scanner yet, enter this address by hand instead:

`{url}`

Webhook ID: `{webhook_id}`

You can bring this code back up any time from the integration's **Configure** button.

error.invalid_webhook_id: Use 8 to 64 letters, numbers, hyphens or underscores.
error.webhook_id_in_use: Something else in Home Assistant already uses that webhook ID — usually a webhook trigger in configuration.yaml. Pick a different one.
error.custom_url_required: Fill in the custom address, or pick one of the other options.
error.invalid_url: That doesn't look like a web address. It needs to start with http:// or https:// followed by your Home Assistant's host name.
error.url_unavailable: That address is no longer available. Pick another one.

abort.already_configured: That webhook ID is already in use by another person.
